transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Ever since the car accident last week, I keep reliving it over and over in my head, even when I’m trying to work or relax, and I can’t seem to shut it off. It feels like it's completely taking over my life, and I just don't know how to make it stop.
Since the car accident, have these symptoms lasted less than a month or more than a month? Also, are you having nightmares, flashbacks, or avoiding reminders of the accident?

It has been six days since the accident, so just under a week. I’m not really having nightmares, but I get these vivid flashbacks during the day where I feel like I'm trapped in the car again, and I'm actively avoiding anything that reminds me of it, like refusing to drive or even talk about road trips.

During the accident or afterward, did you ever feel numb, detached from yourself or your surroundings, or like things weren’t real? Have these symptoms stayed only within the first month since the accident?

Yes, I keep getting this strange, floaty feeling where my surroundings look far away and unreal, and it feels like I'm watching myself from over my shoulder. I also feel completely flat and emotionally disconnected, like I can't access any real warmth or joy. Since the accident was just six days ago, these feelings have been constant all week.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed trauma-related symptoms within 1 week of a serious car accident, including intrusive recollections/flashbacks, avoidance of reminders, dissociative symptoms (derealization, depersonalization), and emotional numbing. Symptoms are confirmed to be within the first month after the trauma, supporting an acute stress reaction/acute stress disorder-spectrum presentation rather than PTSD.
